strongest_angle: Detailing the discovery of dwarf planet candidate 2026 ED138 by the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory, orbiting at roughly 46 times the Earth-sun distance with a 25-degree orbital tilt.

key_facts.fact: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory discovered dwarf planet candidate 2026 ED138 in the outer reaches of the solar system beyond Pluto, as announced on October 27, 2026.
Scientists at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian noted that the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center announced the observations of 2026 ED138 on October 27, 2026.

According to Live Science, the potential dwarf planet 2026 ED138 orbits the sun at roughly 46 times the distance between Earth and the sun with an orbit tilted at a 25-degree angle from the solar system plane.
Mario Jurić, Rubin’s solar system lead scientist at the University of Washington, combed through Rubin and Blanco 4-meter telescope data leading to the discovery.
